target.statement: ADASYN 1x augmentation achieves test AUC of 0.6778 (Gini 0.3557) on the Give Me Some Credit dataset, vs baseline AUC 0.6727
target.dataset: Give Me Some Credit (Kaggle), 97,243 obs after cleaning, 7.07% default rate

compute.basis: XGBoost (100 trees, depth 6) on ~73k rows x 6 features plus ADASYN/SMOTE resampling and 1000-iteration bootstrap on 29k test rows is minutes of CPU work; main cost is downloading the Kaggle dataset and writing the pipeline from scratch since no code is released.

blockers: No code released (paper promises a future GitHub repo but links none)
Kaggle dataset requires a free account/API token to download
Preprocessing caps/outlier rules are only loosely described, so exact AUC may not match to 4 decimals
title: Finding the Sweet Spot: Optimal Data Augmentation Ratio for Imbalanced Credit Scoring Using ADASYN
